title: InferA: A Smart Assistant for Cosmological Ensemble Data
problem: Analyzing large-scale scientific datasets (terabyte-scale) is hindered by volume, structural complexity, and need for domain expertise; existing automation tools (PandasAI) require full ingestion and lack structural awareness.
method: InferA: multi-agent system using LLMs to orchestrate analysis. Supervisor agent coordinates specialized agents for data retrieval and analysis phases; engages users interactively to clarify intent.

title: 3D-SubG: A 3D Stacked Hybrid Processing Near/In-Memory Accelerator for Subgraph GNNs
problem: Subgraph Graph Neural Networks have complex irregular structures with numerous independent subgraphs, creating severe bandwidth bottlenecks and poor data reuse in conventional architectures, limiting throughput.
method: 3D stacks logic die with DRAM die via hybrid bonding; logic die employs SRAM-based processing-in-memory macros for computation density; bit-level non-zero gathering exploits graph sparsity; workload-balanced mapping allocates subgraphs to logic-DRAM blocks; distributed global pooling reduces inter-block data movements.

title: Advancing Rehabilitation Through Low Weight Hand Assistive System: Design and Impact Analysis
problem: Individuals with impaired hand function due to stroke, spinal cord injuries, and neuromuscular disorders struggle with daily activities and rehabilitation. Existing assistive devices are often slow and lack real-time feedback.
method: Smart Hand Mobility Assistive Device integrating: (1) Advanced sensor technology for finger movement detection, (2) Real-time data processing for immediate feedback, (3) Adaptive actuation for motor amplification. Mobile application provides physiotherapy exercises and interactive therapeutic games. Multiple control modes: manual assistance, cyclic training, task-specific routines.

title: Protecting Cryptographic Code Against Spectre-RSB: (and, in Fact, All Known Spectre Variants)
problem: Constant-time cryptographic code is designed to prevent timing-based secret leakage, but Spectre attacks—especially Spectre-RSB (Return Stack Buffer)—can violate constant-time guarantees by leaking secrets during speculative execution, and prior defenses cover only Spectre-v1 while leaving other Spectre variants unaddressed.
method: The approach combines a new value-dependent information-flow type system with a compiler transformation. The type system statically tracks whether values depend on secrets and whether they may flow to speculative-execution leak channels (cache, port contention, etc.) under any of the known Spectre mistraining variants. The compiler transformation rewrites low-level code to enforce the type-system restrictions—inserting fences, reordering, and masking as needed—so that no secret-dependent value reaches a speculative leak channel. Both the type-system soundness and the correctness of the compiler transformation are machine-proved in the Coq proof assistant, then implemented in the Jasmin high-assurance cryptography framework.

title: Cinnamon: A Framework for Scale-Out Encrypted AI
problem: Fully homomorphic encryption (FHE) imposes orders-of-magnitude performance overhead for ML inference, and prior FHE accelerators use massive monolithic chip designs that do not scale to large models like BERT and provide poor performance-per-dollar.
method: Cinnamon is a scale-out FHE acceleration framework that exploits parallelism at all program levels using novel algorithms, a compiler, and a chiplet-based hardware design. The compiler identifies and schedules FHE operation parallelism (polynomial NTT, RNS decomposition, key-switching) across multiple chips, while architectural extensions reduce per-chip resource requirements to enable economical scaling. Novel algorithms reduce communication volume between chiplets, enabling a distributed multi-chip FHE accelerator rather than a single monolithic die.

title: AMALI: An Analytical Model for Accurately Modeling LLM Inference on Modern GPUs
problem: Existing GPU analytical models cannot accurately predict LLM inference performance because they mismodel tensor core throughput, ignore constant and instruction cache effects, and abstract away warp-level execution details critical to LLM kernels.
method: AMALI introduces three modeling innovations: (1) an instruction-modifier and throughput-based tensor core model that captures math-pipe throttle stalls by accurately modeling the pipeline fill/drain behavior of tensor cores; (2) micro-benchmark-derived analytical models for constant cache and instruction cache that measure CUDA kernel launching latencies; (3) a multi-warp model using warp instruction number distributions to reflect the heterogeneous occupancy and scheduling behavior of LLM inference kernels. All three components are validated against real A100 hardware measurements.

title: A Wireless Adiabatic Stimulator System with Current-Mode Power Reception and Stimulus Current Regulation Achieving Precise Charge Delivery and Electrode Scalability for Miniaturized Electroceuticals
problem: Miniaturized wireless neurostimulators must deliver precise charge with high power conversion efficiency (PCE) and high stimulation efficiency factor (SEF) while maintaining electrode scalability; as receiver coil shrinks, received power decreases, and electrode-tissue impedance (ETI) increases, degrading both PCE and charge delivery accuracy.
method: Current-mode power receiver with integrated stimulus current regulation achieves dual objectives: (1) direct current-mode conversion maintains high efficiency across variable ETI without requiring separate voltage regulation; (2) closed-loop stimulus current feedback provides precise charge delivery independent of electrode impedance variation. Design inherently supports electrode scalability by tolerating high ETI voltages (V_T) while maintaining constant output current regardless of load impedance.

title: LiquidGEMM: Hardware-Efficient W4A8 GEMM Kernel for High-Performance LLM Serving
problem: Quantization accelerates LLM inference by reducing memory and computation. W4A8 (4-bit weights, 8-bit activations) balances accuracy-performance tradeoff, but existing GEMM kernels suffer inefficient dequantization on CUDA Cores, unable to match Tensor Core throughput.
method: LiquidGEMM hardware-efficient W4A8 GEMM kernel with two key techniques: (1) LiquidQuant - hardware-efficient quantization using 2 arithmetic instructions per 4 elements, enabling overflow-safe dequantization, (2) Implicit fine-grained pipeline overlapping weight loading, dequantization, and MMA across warp groups without synchronization or redundant memory traffic.

title: GSIM: Accelerating RTL Simulation for Large-Scale Designs
problem: Software RTL simulation is a major bottleneck in hardware design; simulation of complex processors and systems exhibits high computational overhead in multiple layers (supernode, node, and bit levels).
method: GSIM identifies and optimizes computational overhead across three levels: supernode-level optimizations for high-level logic, node-level techniques for gate-level operations, and bit-level optimizations for bitwise computation. Combines these with efficient data structures and scheduling to accelerate simulation of complex processors.

title: KAMI: Communication-Avoiding General Matrix Multiplication within a Single GPU
problem: Large-scale GEMM near peak GPU performance, but substantial optimization opportunities remain in small and batched GEMM operations.
method: KAMI: 1D/2D/3D communication-avoiding GEMM algorithms optimizing at thread block level; utilizes tensor cores, thread registers, shared memory; includes SpMM and SpGEMM variants.

title: Einsum Trees: An Abstraction for Optimizing the Execution of Tensor Expressions
problem: Optimizing the execution of multi-operand einsum tensor expressions requires co-optimizing both the contraction path (order of binary contractions) and the data layout of intermediate tensors, but these two problems have been studied in isolation, leading to suboptimal global execution performance.
method: The paper introduces Einsum Tree IR, an intermediate representation that captures a full contraction path as a tree structure, enabling global optimization of tensor data layouts across all intermediate binary contractions simultaneously rather than locally per contraction. Given a contraction path (computed by existing algorithms), Einsum Tree IR applies global data-layout optimization to minimize data movement and improve cache utilization. The resulting optimized sequences of binary contractions are executed on general-purpose server CPUs (Arm and x86) using existing optimized BLAS/tensor kernels.

title: Reproducibility Report for SC25 Paper CPU- and GPU-initiated Communication Strategies for Conjugate Gradient Methods on Large GPU Clusters
problem: Artifact evaluation and reproducibility verification of communication strategy research for CG methods on GPU clusters.
method: Artifact evaluation following SC25 guidelines for CPU- and GPU-initiated communication strategies.

title: Qonductor: A Cloud Orchestrator for Quantum Computing
problem: Hybrid quantum-classical applications face challenges in resource management and job scheduling across heterogeneous hybrid resources, with no unified abstraction for programming and orchestration.
method: Qonductor cloud orchestrator with high-level hardware-agnostic API, resource estimator for quantum-classical balancing, and hybrid scheduler optimizing QoS/efficiency trade-offs across quantum and classical resources.

title: 34.2 A 380μW and -242.8dB FoM Digital-PLL-Based GFSK Modulator with Sub-20μs Settling Frequency Hopping for Bluetooth Low-Energy in 22nm CMOS
problem: Ultra-low-power Bluetooth Low-Energy (BLE) transceivers must support GFSK modulation and adaptive frequency hopping (2.402-2.480GHz) with sub-20μs settling time while minimizing power dissipation, but existing DPLL-based approaches struggle with the power/noise/hopping-speed trade-off.
method: Digital-PLL-based GFSK modulator using dynamic-tuning-curve tracking and optimized DCO design to manage frequency modulation, hopping, and PVT variations with reduced switched-capacitor banks, achieving 380μW power at -242.8dB FoM with sub-20μs frequency hopping.

title: Evaluating HPK for Running Cloud-Native Workloads on Slurm Clusters
problem: Integrating cloud-native and HPC workloads requires separate resources; leads to inefficient resource partitioning
method: HPK framework enabling unmodified cloud-native workload execution on main HPC cluster (Slurm)

title: Classification of Three-dimensional Electron Diffraction Data with a Large Language Model
problem: Three-dimensional electron diffraction (3D ED) generates hundreds to thousands of molecular structures per sample, but many are inaccurate due to noise and measurement limitations. Manual inspection is time-consuming and labor-intensive.
method: LLM-centric automatic screening method: (1) converts atomic coordinates to topology-only language representation, (2) applies rule-based filtering, (3) fine-tunes LLM on correct vs. artificially-corrupted molecules, (4) groups identical topologies.
